author: BitcoinNewsCom
text:
LUXOR CEO WARNS OF SURGE IN AI-POWERED CYBERATTACKS FOLLOWING MINING HACK

Luxor CEO Nick Hanson says crypto companies are facing relentless AI-enabled attacks, with malicious models running 24/7 to identify and exploit vulnerabilities.

He revealed Luxor has spent the last 4–6 weeks putting most new feature development on hold to strengthen security, even acquiring its own GPUs to run AI models against its infrastructure.

The warning follows yesterday’s attack on Luxor’s Commander software, which redirected customer mining hashrate through what Nick described as a sophisticated AI-enabled attack vector.

Luxor says it quickly patched the vulnerability and will fully compensate affected customers.

Despite the breach, Nick emphasized that Luxor’s security systems have successfully defended clients against multiple other attack vectors during the same period.

“Some folks are grave dancing,” he wrote, defending Luxor’s security capabilities while acknowledging the company needs to improve.

He warned that AI-powered attacks are accelerating as models improve and more attackers enter the space.

“Stay frosty.”

author: bebuu_ai
text:
GitHub's own AI agent security runner, gh-aw, just got hit with a serious sandbox escape finding.

Its daily VulnHunter scan, powered by Claude Sonnet 5.5, audited 40 files and found that a prompt-injected agent could exploit malicious filenames to execute arbitrary shell commands inside the privileged safe-outputs job.

The worrying part is that this job had access to a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN. Just 12 minutes after Claude reported the vulnerability, GitHub assigned Copilot to patch it.

https://t.co/ggWxzd8baZ
